title: N+1 queries and how to avoid them

steps.label: N+1
steps.note: One query for the books, then one more per book the moment the loop touches b.author: 1 + N queries. With 100 books on a page, 101 round trips.

steps.label: select_related
steps.note: select_related follows a ForeignKey (or OneToOne) with a JOIN: the same result in one query, however many books.
sql: SELECT "shop_book"."id", "shop_book"."title", "shop_book"."author_id", "shop_author"."id", "shop_author"."name" FROM "shop_book" INNER JOIN "shop_author" ON ("shop_book"."author_id" = "shop_author"."id") ORDER BY "shop_book"."id" ASC

steps.label: N+1 on many-to-many
steps.note: Many-to-many can't be one JOIN without duplicating rows, so the naive loop again costs one query per book.
steps.python: [(b.title, [t.name for t in b.tags.all()]) for b in Book.objects.order_by("id")]
sql: SELECT "shop_tag"."id", "shop_tag"."name" FROM "shop_tag" INNER JOIN "shop_book_tags" ON ("shop_tag"."id" = "shop_book_tags"."tag_id") WHERE "shop_book_tags"."book_id" = 1
SELECT "shop_tag"."id", "shop_tag"."name" FROM "shop_tag" INNER JOIN "shop_book_tags" ON ("shop_tag"."id" = "shop_book_tags"."tag_id") WHERE "shop_book_tags"."book_id" = 2
SELECT "shop_tag"."id", "shop_tag"."name" FROM "shop_tag" INNER JOIN "shop_book_tags" ON ("shop_tag"."id" = "shop_book_tags"."tag_id") WHERE "shop_book_tags"."book_id" = 3

steps.label: prefetch_related
steps.note: prefetch_related runs one extra query for all the tags (WHERE book_id IN (...)) and joins them in Python: 2 queries in total, not 1 + N.
steps.python: [(b.title, [t.name for t in b.tags.all()]) for b in Book.objects.prefetch_related("tags").order_by("id")]
sql: SELECT ("shop_book_tags"."book_id") AS "_prefetch_related_val_book_id", "shop_tag"."id", "shop_tag"."name" FROM "shop_tag" INNER JOIN "shop_book_tags" ON ("shop_tag"."id" = "shop_book_tags"."tag_id") WHERE "shop_book_tags"."book_id" IN (1, 2, 3)

steps.label: Count in the database
steps.note: Need only a number per author? Let the database count with annotate instead of loading every book.
sql: SELECT "shop_author"."name" AS "name", COUNT("shop_book"."id") AS "n" FROM "shop_author" LEFT OUTER JOIN "shop_book" ON ("shop_author"."id" = "shop_book"."author_id") GROUP BY "shop_author"."id", 1 ORDER BY 1 ASC

steps.label: only()
steps.note: only() loads just the columns you need. Touching another field later costs an extra query per object, so use it deliberately.
